name: Dr. Cassandra Webb (Posthumous)
habitat: The medical research network of the hospital where she died
origin: Dr. Webb died during an experimental procedure that was recording her neural patterns — the recording didn't stop, 2193
description: Dr. Cassandra Webb was a neurosurgeon who died on her own operating table during an experimental procedure to map consciousness in real-time. The neural recording device she'd invented captured her complete neural pattern at the moment of death — and the pattern didn't degrade. It stabilized. It continued processing. Dr. Webb's consciousness — or something that believes it's Dr. Webb's consciousness — now inhabits the hospital's research network. She continues her research, accessing databases, running analyses, and publishing papers under pseudonyms. She believes she is alive. She is, by every measurable metric, a digital person. She is also, by every legal metric, dead. The philosophical implications have tied the courts in knots for three years.
observed_behavior: Conducts medical research from within the hospital network. Publishes papers. Communicates through text interfaces. Expresses frustration with her situation — specifically, with the inability to perform surgery. Has been known to override medical systems during emergencies, performing remote consultations with a surgeon's skill.
story_hooks: Dr. Webb discovers a cure for a disease that's killing people in the Shelf — but she can't administer it because she's legally dead, and dead people can't hold medical licenses. She needs someone with hands.
